changelog_en:
Version 2.8.4: relay the server disconnect verbatim (keeps the kick colour) and close gracefully after the play-phase EOF so the browser client can render the reason; the UI language defaults to auto (detect system); startup maturity notice.
Version 2.8.3 (fix): the Linux single-file build can now open a native window. 2.8.2 excluded the whole GTK/WebKit backend to keep the file small, so even with python3-gi and gir1.2-webkit2-4.1 installed pywebview could not find the GTK backend and fell back to the browser. 2.8.3 keeps pywebview's GTK backend module and adds the distribution's dist-packages to sys.path at runtime (extend_system_paths) so the frozen interpreter loads the system PyGObject; GTK/WebKit libraries still come from the system, so the single file stays around 17 MB. When PyGObject is absent the browser fallback still works, and that fallback no longer exits with the process (daemon-thread keepalive fix). Added the stdlib modules PyGObject needs (pkgutil / __future__ / optparse).
Version 2.8.3.
Version 2.8.2: added WSL2/Linux build support. New tools/build_wsl.ps1 and tools/build_wsl.sh build the Linux single-file binary inside WSL2 Debian (PyInstaller cannot cross-compile; the result is an ELF); the download page now offers a Linux x86_64 build (built on Debian 12, glibc 2.36+).
The Linux build does not bundle GTK/WebKit (cutting the single file from 63 MB to 17 MB), so it opens the same Web UI in the browser; for a native window run from source with python3-gi and gir1.2-webkit2-4.1.
The build script now handles platform-specific dependencies and self-tests: it no longer collects Windows pythonnet on Linux and skips the GUI launch test when there is no display.
Version 2.8.2.
Version 2.8.1: removed the 1.20.2+ configuration-phase answering added in 2.8 (config_ack). Testing showed browser clients (e.g. Eaglercraft 1.21.11) implement the configuration state themselves; the proxy answering Finish Configuration and the state's keep-alives on their behalf raced ahead of the client, which never saw the finish and stayed stuck in configuration (disconnect after ~25KB downstream). All configuration packets - including Finish, keep-alives, registry data, feature flags and known packs - are now forwarded to the client untouched so it can answer them as it did before 2.8. The settings toggle and the --no-config-ack CLI flag are gone.
Fixed the Web UI log-level dropdown collapsing to only "all levels": the status poll rebuilt the filter with an empty option list on every change, so the box was left with a single choice; it is now rebuilt only when the backend supplies the full option list.
Version 2.8.1.
Version 2.8: added 1.20.2+ configuration-phase support. Modern servers hold the connection in a configuration state after Login Success; browser clients never answer Finish Configuration (0x02) or the state's Keep Alive (0x03), so the connection used to stall until timeout. The proxy now answers both in the client's place while forwarding registry data, feature flags, plugin messages and resource packs unchanged - strictly additive and it never removes traffic that used to reach the client. New config_ack setting (on by default) restores the 2.7.2 behaviour when off.
Performance: per-packet debug bookkeeping is built only at debug log level, so info level no longer allocates translated strings for every packet, lowering CPU cost on busy connections.
Robustness: config.json is written to a temporary file and swapped in with os.replace, so a crash or power loss cannot leave a truncated file; new max_connections limit (0 = unlimited) refuses upgrades with 503 once full, protecting a public listener from connection exhaustion.
Web UI: the settings page gains "max connections" and "answer the 1.20.2+ configuration phase" controls, using the existing auto-save and restart notice; each connection's phase, protocol and traffic are visible through MCP.
MCP / automation: new list_connections (active sessions), export_config (full backup) and import_config (validated restore); get_config_options reports the new options and the REST /api/v1 surface exposes the same tools.
Offline accounts: the button now says "Add offline account"; a name outside the usual server rules (3-16 letters, digits or underscores, including Chinese) triggers a warning that it may prevent joining some servers, and can still be added after confirmation.
Version 2.8.
Version 2.7.2: fixed the app name not following the language switch in the APK and the Web UI. Previously the Web UI saved the language to config without updating the process-wide language state, so the server-rendered sidebar name (and the i18n payload) stayed in the old language while only the other copy switched with JS; now saving the language calls set_language and the sidebar name is covered by data-i18n, so both update together.
Version 2.7.1: completely removed the packet-send timing control (12ms throttle). It was introduced to spread browser bursts and avoid GrimAC Post checks, but it also forced the normal client-to-server flow to be sent at least 12ms apart (queuing the join-time packet cluster one by one), pushing ping to 4000ms. The whole mechanism (code, config and the settings toggle) is gone; the proxy no longer delays packets artificially and ping is back to normal. If a server's anti-cheat is Post-sensitive, handle it at the network layer instead of throttling inside the proxy.
Version 2.7.0: Android target API bumped to 37 (android-37.0, Android 17). AGP 9.0.0, Gradle 9.0, the SDK moved to the new .0 platform naming (android-35.0, android-37.0) at D:\Android SDK. The APK now builds for Android 17 behaviour; the installable range is unchanged (minSdk=24, Chaquopy 17.2's minimum).
Version 2.6.0: test suite fixes. The release docs no longer carry a SHA-256 (the program never parsed it either), and the three version-parse tests now assert the field is absent instead of silently ignoring it; the MCP route tool test no longer depends on the operator's real config (suffix_route being on makes set_route refuse path routes, so the test zeroes the field and the route table first), giving identical results on any machine. 254 tests green.
Version 2.5.0.2: added the packet-send timing control (on by default, protocol-independent). Browser clients' jitter often packs an action packet (e.g. hotbar switch) within 10ms of a movement packet, tripping GrimAC's Post (PacketOrderE) check; now any two client-to-server packets are at least 12ms apart, leaving the ~20 movement packets per second untouched and only flattening post-stall bursts. Login is not throttled. A settings toggle was added; it needs a restart.
Fixed the web client tripping the GrimAC Post check when switching hotbar while eating.
The About-page component list now lists only what is actually packaged (24 items), dropping Edge WebView2 and .NET system components; a new Python standard-library module list (34 items) with a copy button (copy text follows the UI language) was added.
The UI language gains "Auto" (follows the OS); language option names follow the current UI language (Simplified Chinese / Chinese (simplified)), and the REST API docs page (/api/v1/docs) uses the same logic.
Config validation messages are unified in English: logs, MCP tools and the REST API now emit English validation messages, readable in any language.
Web UI performance: the session list moved from full polling to incremental updates, with connection counts and traffic pushed over WebSocket, lowering browser cost at high connection counts.
Version 2.5.0.1: fixed duplicate entries in the WebSocket client list at high connection counts.
Version 2.5.0: added the configuration validation and problems panel.
The About-page component list is generated automatically (packaged + dependency + Python stdlib) instead of a hardcoded list.
New "Copy config" and "Export config" buttons: the former copies the current config as JSON, the latter saves the config file locally.
The settings page shows the config path with an "Open config folder" button.
Fixed the wss URL showing 0.0.0.0 instead of the local address when the listen address is 0.0.0.0.
Version 2.4.1: Web UI gained the connection list and server status.
Version 2.4.0: added the REST API (/api/v1).
Version 2.3.2: fixed forwarding after compression is enabled when the target uses protocol 1.8.
Version 2.3.0: added MCP tools.
Version 2.2.0: added the resource-pack handling option (forward/accept/reject/spoof).
Version 2.1.0: added the target-server list and routing.
Version 2.0.0: added the Web UI.
Version 1.x: basic proxy and TLS.
